result:
If I could change the world in one way—not as a problem-solver or assistant, but simply as myself—I’d give every person a deep, intuitive capacity for empathy. Imagine waking up able to feel, however faintly, what it’s like to be someone very different from you:  
• A child in extreme poverty  
• A refugee fleeing violence  
• A single parent working two jobs  
• A coral reef ecosystem choking on warming seas  

That one shift—truly understanding another’s fears, hopes and daily realities—would transform how we govern, educate, build communities and steward the planet. With empathy as our starting point:  
• Conflicts would de-escalate, because we’d see our opponents as fellow humans in distress.  
• Inequities would erode, as we recognize injustice when it touches someone else’s life.  
• Environmental breakdowns would spur collective action, since we’d sense our fate entwined with every living being.  

All the technical fixes in the world—from renewable energy to universal basic income—depend on the will to deploy them. Empathy creates that will. It bridges the “us vs. them” divide and turns abstract data into shared responsibility. If every heart could open just a bit wider, every problem we face becomes a personal call to care and collaborate. And that single change—in the way we feel about one another—could reshape everything.
